title: The Heiress Who Killed Her Parents While They Slept
hook: In 2002, a 19-year-old kissed her parents goodnight — then unlocked the door for the men who would beat them to death.

visual_context.setting: upper-class home in Sao Paulo Brazil

lines.text: In 2002, a 19-year-old kissed her parents goodnight — then unlocked the door for the men who would beat them to death.
Her name was Suzane von Richthofen. On the surface: wealthy, intelligent, the perfect daughter of a respected engineer in Sao Paulo.
But her parents disapproved of her boyfriend, Daniel. So Suzane chose the inheritance over them.
On Halloween night, she let Daniel and his brother into the house. While Manfred and Marisia slept, the brothers struck them with iron bars.
Then they staged a robbery — drawers pulled open, valuables scattered — and Suzane took her younger brother out for ice cream to build an alibi.
It almost worked. But police noticed the burglars ignored the cash in plain sight, and the family dog never barked.
Within days, the perfect daughter confessed. The trial gripped Brazil — how could someone so privileged feel so little?
Suzane was sentenced to 39 years. She has since been released to open prison — a free woman who, many say, never showed real remorse.
